title: Maximum space on one tape under composition
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, with state sets $S_1$ and $S_2$, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Form a machine on $S_1\sqcup S_2$ that follows $M_1$ on left states, switches from the specified exit state to the specified entry state in one step without changing the tapes, and follows $M_2$ on right states. Suppose $M_1$ takes $(start,w_0)$ to $(exit,w_1)$ after $T_1$ steps, without visiting $exit$ earlier, and $M_2$ takes $(entry,w_1)$ to $(q_2,w_2)$ after $T_2$ steps. For each work tape $i$, if either the set of cells visited by its head in the first run through time $T_1$ or the set visited in the second run through time $T_2$ is exactly the singleton consisting of cell $0$, then the composed run through time $T_1+1+T_2$ visits at most the maximum of the two runs' visited-cell counts on tape $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1,M_2$ are machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet
$M_1$ does not have state $exit$ at any earlier time $t<T_1$
Either the first run's visited-cell set on tape $i$ through $T_1$ is $\{0\}$ or the second run's visited-cell set through $T_2$ is $\{0\}$
